To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the face to face collaborative learning environment is more conducive to collaborative learning, and is more conducive to the learning of the students.
the asynchronous online forum can be a powerful collaborative learning environment, and that it is a very different learning environment to face to face.

students in the asynchronous online group had more opportunities to participate and contribute to the collaborative learning process than those in the face-to-face group, but that the face to face group were more likely to be engaged in collaborative learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact on learning of the use of asynchronous on-line communication in a subject where the traditional form of collaborative work is through the face to face group.
how students collaborate with each other, in both face to face, and online, asynchronous environments.
the differences in the way students communicate and collaborate in a face to face and an on line environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the online form of communication provides a student centric, collaborative learning environment, which is not available in face to face communication.
the two methods of collaborative communication have very different impacts upon collaborative learning.
there is no difference between the two modes of communication, as the collaborative learning process is the same in both cases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the asynchronous online forum provides a different form of collaborative learning, with its asynchronous, student centric, written form.
the asynchronous online form of communication provides a more student centric collaborative learning environment.
face to face collaborative learning is more effective than asynchronous online collaborative learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both forms of communication have a place, but the asynchronous online form is more conducive to a deeper form of learning.
the asynchronous online communication is not a substitute for the traditional collaborative learning environment.
the two forms of communication have different effects on collaborative learning and that the two forms should be considered as complementary, not as competing.
